skill.name: hig-patterns
skill.description: Guides Apple app interaction decisions using Human Interface Guidelines references for onboarding, loading, modality, feedback, account flows, media, notifications, search, settings, and related UX patterns.
skill.summary: Select Apple HIG interaction patterns and explain the rationale for app flows.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Apple app teams need fast guidance when choosing interaction patterns across onboarding, loading, feedback, and permissions. This skill maps design questions to Apple HIG reference topics and practical implementation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Apple HIG patterns for onboarding, launch, loading, modality, feedback, search, settings, media, notifications, and account flows.
Maps user goals to recommended patterns and anti-patterns from the pattern selection guide.
Provides step-by-step implementation guidance for screens, states, and interaction moments.
Cites relevant reference files when explaining a recommendation.
Highlights platform variations and common HIG pitfalls for Apple app experiences.
limitations: It is design guidance, not a complete App Store review or legal compliance check.
It does not include all foundation, layout, component, or platform rules from related HIG skills.
It needs app context, target platforms, and the surrounding user flow for precise recommendations.
Reference material may lag changes in the latest Apple Human Interface Guidelines.

use_cases.title: Review an onboarding flow
use_cases.description: Use the skill to reduce onboarding steps, defer sign-in, and place permission requests at useful moments.

use_cases.title: Choose an interaction pattern
use_cases.description: Use the skill to compare modal, inline, undo, feedback, search, loading, or settings patterns for a feature.

use_cases.title: Align product requirements with HIG
use_cases.description: Use the skill to turn product goals into Apple platform interaction guidance and common pitfalls.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a pattern
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one flow decision.
prompt_templates.prompt: Recommend the best Apple HIG pattern for my [flow]. The app is [type], platforms are [platforms], and users need [task].

prompt_templates.title: Audit a flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of an existing experience.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this [onboarding/loading/permission/settings] flow against Apple HIG patterns. List the strongest issues, recommended changes, and reference files.

prompt_templates.title: Design state guidance
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for multiple screens or states.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design HIG-aligned interaction guidance for [feature]. Cover entry state, empty state, loading, errors, feedback, undo, and platform variations.

prompt_templates.title: Compare alternatives
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced tradeoff analysis for product or design review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these interaction options for [feature]: [option A] and [option B]. Explain HIG tradeoffs, risks, and the preferred implementation path.

output_examples.input: A designer asks how onboarding should work for a finance app on iPhone and iPad.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends brief onboarding, deferred sign-in, contextual permission requests, and platform notes for iPhone and iPad layouts.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether a destructive file action needs a confirmation dialog.
output_examples.output: The skill weighs undo support against confirmation, explains when confirmation is still needed, and cites file management or modality guidance.

output_examples.input: A product manager asks why a loading screen feels slow and disruptive.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests useful placeholders, determinate progress when possible, reduced blocking states, and clearer feedback during long operations.

best_practices: Provide the target platforms, previous screen, next screen, and any sensitive actions in the prompt.
Ask for rationale tied to specific reference files when making product or design decisions.
Validate final decisions against current Apple documentation before launch.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for only visual styling advice when the decision is about interaction behavior.
Do not omit platform details for flows that differ across iOS, macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, tvOS, or visionOS.
Do not treat the guidance as App Store approval, legal advice, or accessibility certification.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose Apple HIG interaction patterns for app flows, feedback, loading, modality, search, settings, media, and account experiences.

faq.question: Does it write production UI code?
faq.answer: No. It provides design and implementation guidance that developers can translate into platform code.

faq.question: Which Apple platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers patterns used across iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS when the reference files include those notes.

faq.question: Can it review an existing flow?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current screens, target users, platform, and known issues so it can identify HIG conflicts.

faq.question: Does it replace Apple documentation?
faq.answer: No. It summarizes and applies bundled references, but teams should verify final choices with current Apple documentation.

faq.question: How should I get the best answer?
faq.answer: Describe the user goal, platform, flow entry point, exit point, sensitive actions, and any constraints.
